title: Feelings and judgements: me alegra que, es importante que
summary: React to what other people do with me alegra que, me preocupa que, es importante que + the present subjunctive, and use the infinitive when nobody new is involved.
focus: The present subjunctive after feelings and value judgements
content:
## Feelings about someone else: me alegra que…

When you react to what **someone else** does, the action after **que** goes in the present subjunctive.

- **Me alegra que vengas.** I'm glad you're coming.
- **Me molesta que fumes.** It bothers me that you smoke.
- **Me preocupa que no comas.** It worries me that you don't eat.
- **Me da pena que te vayas.** It makes me sad that you're leaving.
- **Me encanta que me escribas.** I love it that you write to me.
- **Odio que llegues tarde.** I hate it when you're late.

**Alegrar, preocupar, dar pena**… work like **gustar**: the pronoun shows who feels (**le preocupa que**, **nos alegra que**). **Odiar** is ordinary: **odio, odias, odia…**

## Judgements: es importante que…

**Es** + an adjective or noun works the same way. When a specific person is meant, add **que** + subjunctive:

- **Es importante que descanses.** It's important that you rest.
- **Es necesario que firméis aquí.** You need to sign here.
- **Es mejor que vayamos en tren.** It's better if we go by train.
- **Es normal que estés nervioso.** It's normal for you to be nervous.
- **Es una pena que no puedas venir.** It's a shame you can't come.
- **Es increíble que hable cuatro idiomas.** It's amazing that she speaks four languages.

**Estar contento de que** + subjunctive too: **Estoy contenta de que trabajemos juntos.** I'm happy that we work together.

## Same person or everyone: the infinitive

No new subject, no **que**. If the person who feels is the one who acts, or you mean people in general, use the infinitive:

| same person or general | someone else |
|---|---|
| **Me alegra verte.** I'm glad to see you. | **Me alegra que me visites.** I'm glad you visit me. |
| **Odio esperar.** I hate waiting. | **Odio que me hagas esperar.** I hate it when you make me wait. |
| **Es importante dormir.** Sleep is important. | **Es importante que duermas.** It's important that you sleep. |
| **Estoy contento de estar aquí.** | **Estoy contento de que estés aquí.** |

So **me alegra verte**, never *me alegra que te veo*.

## Even when it is true

This subjunctive is not about doubt. In **me da pena que estés enfermo** I know you are ill; the subjunctive marks my *reaction* to the fact.

- **Sé que estás enfermo.** I know you're ill. (stating a fact takes the indicative)
- **Me da pena que estés enfermo.** I'm sorry you're ill. (reacting takes the subjunctive)
- **Veo que llueve.** I see it's raining. Compare **Es una pena que llueva.** It's a shame it's raining.

At B1 the present subjunctive covers what happens now or later. Reacting to something already done (**me alegra que hayas venido**) comes at B2.

vocabulary.meaning: I'm glad that, it makes me happy that
vocabulary.example: Me alegra que estés mejor.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm glad you're better.

vocabulary.meaning: it bothers me that, it annoys me that
vocabulary.example: Me molesta que mi vecino ponga la música tan alta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It annoys me that my neighbour plays music so loud.

vocabulary.example: Me preocupa que mi abuelo viva solo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It worries me that my grandfather lives alone.

vocabulary.meaning: it makes me sad that, I'm sorry that
vocabulary.example: Me da pena que te vayas tan pronto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It makes me sad that you're leaving so soon.

vocabulary.example: Me encanta que mis amigos me visiten.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I love it when my friends visit me.

vocabulary.example: Odio que me interrumpan cuando hablo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hate it when people interrupt me while I'm talking.

vocabulary.example: Es importante que leas el contrato.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's important that you read the contract.

vocabulary.example: Es necesario que traigáis el pasaporte.
vocabulary.example_meaning: You need to bring your passports.

vocabulary.meaning: it's better that, it's better if
vocabulary.example: Es mejor que salgamos temprano.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's better if we leave early.

vocabulary.example: Es normal que los bebés lloren.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's normal for babies to cry.

vocabulary.example: Es una pena que no sepas nadar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's a shame you can't swim.

vocabulary.meaning: it's amazing that, it's unbelievable that

vocabulary.example_meaning: It's amazing that the train is on time.

vocabulary.example: Estoy contenta de que mi hija estudie medicina.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm happy that my daughter is studying medicine.

quiz.prompt: Me molesta que tú siempre ___ tarde.
quiz.explanation: A feeling about what someone else does: me molesta que + subjunctive. Llegar becomes llegue, with -gu- to keep the hard g: que llegues.
hints: Two different people: me (I'm annoyed) and tú (you arrive).
-gar verbs write -gue in the subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Me preocupa que mi hermano no ___ (dormir) bien.
quiz.explanation: Me preocupa que + subjunctive, because the brother is a different subject. Dormir keeps its o to ue change in the él form: duerma.
hints: Present subjunctive, él form.
Build it on the yo present (o to ue) with the opposite vowel.

quiz.prompt: Es una pena que el restaurante no ___ (abrir) los lunes.
quiz.explanation: Es una pena que + subjunctive. Abrir is a regular -ir verb, so it takes the 'opposite' -a ending: abra.
hints: A judgement about a specific thing takes que + subjunctive.
-ir verbs end in -a in the subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Choose the natural way to say 'I'm glad to see you.'
quiz.explanation: The one who is glad is also the one who sees, so there is no new subject and no que: me alegra + infinitive (verte).
hints: Who is glad? Who sees? The same person?

quiz.prompt: Odio que mis vecinos ___ (hacer) ruido por la noche.
quiz.explanation: Odio que + subjunctive when someone else does the thing. Hacer builds its subjunctive on hago: hagan.
hints: Ellos form of the present subjunctive.
Start from hago and swap -o for -a: haga.

quiz.prompt: Sé que estás enfermo, y me da pena que ___ enfermo.
quiz.explanation: Even though the illness is a known fact (sé que estás), a feeling about it takes the subjunctive: me da pena que estés.
hints: The subjunctive marks a reaction, not doubt.

quiz.prompt: Es normal que (vosotros) ___ (estar) nerviosos antes del examen.
quiz.explanation: Es normal que + subjunctive for specific people. Estar in the vosotros subjunctive is estéis, with an accent.
hints: Vosotros form of the present subjunctive.
Estar stresses the ending, so this form carries a written accent.

quiz.prompt: Estoy contento de que mis padres ___ a verme.
quiz.explanation: Estar contento de que + subjunctive: my parents are a different subject, so que vengan (the subjunctive is built on yo vengo).
hints: Who is happy, and who is coming?

quiz.prompt: Es mejor que (tú) ___ (llamar) a tu abuela hoy.
quiz.explanation: Es mejor que + subjunctive for advice to a specific person. Llamar is -ar, so the subjunctive takes -e: llames.
hints: Tú form of the present subjunctive.
-ar verbs switch to -e.

conversations.title: Good news, mixed feelings
conversations.scenario: Javier phones his friend Lucía to tell her he is starting a new job in another city.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Javier! Me alegra mucho que me llames. ¿Qué tal todo?
lines.meaning: Javier! I'm so glad you're calling. How's everything?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Muy bien. Tengo una noticia: empiezo un trabajo nuevo en Bilbao.
lines.meaning: Very well. I've got news: I'm starting a new job in Bilbao.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Enhorabuena! Me encanta que tengas una aventura nueva.
lines.meaning: Congratulations! I love it that you've got a new adventure.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Gracias. Pero me da pena que no vivamos en la misma ciudad.
lines.meaning: Thanks. But it makes me sad that we won't live in the same city.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: A mí también. Es normal que estés un poco nervioso, ¿no?
lines.meaning: Me too. It's normal for you to be a bit nervous, isn't it?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Sí. Me preocupa que los pisos allí sean tan caros.
lines.meaning: Yes. It worries me that flats there are so expensive.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Es mejor que busques con calma. Y es importante descansar antes de empezar.
lines.meaning: It's better if you look calmly. And it's important to rest before you start.
lines.note: a specific person takes que + subjunctive; in general, the infinitive

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Tienes razón. Odio que las mudanzas sean tan largas.
lines.meaning: You're right. I hate how long moving house takes.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Pues es increíble que siempre lo organices todo tan bien.
lines.meaning: Well, it's amazing how you always organise everything so well.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Qué amable! Estoy contento de que seamos amigos.
lines.meaning: How kind! I'm happy that we're friends.

listening.text: Me encanta que cantes tan bien.
listening.meaning: I love it that you sing so well.
listening.note: A feeling about someone else: que + subjunctive.

listening.text: Es importante beber mucha agua.
listening.meaning: It's important to drink lots of water.

listening.text: Nos alegra que vengáis a la boda.
listening.meaning: We're glad you're coming to the wedding.
listening.note: New word: la boda = the wedding.

listening.text: Me preocupa que el niño tenga fiebre otra vez.
listening.meaning: It worries me that the boy has a temperature again.
listening.note: We know he has it; the worry still takes the subjunctive.

listening.text: Es increíble que no llueva nunca en agosto.
listening.meaning: It's amazing that it never rains in August.

listening.text: Es una pena que mis primos vivan tan lejos del pueblo.
listening.meaning: It's a shame my cousins live so far from the village.
listening.note: New word: el pueblo = the village.

listening.text: Mi madre está contenta de que yo busque trabajo en Valencia.
listening.meaning: My mother is happy that I'm looking for work in Valencia.

listening.text: A mi hermana le molesta que sus compañeros no limpien nunca la cocina.
listening.meaning: It annoys my sister that her flatmates never clean the kitchen.

guide.tip: Ask two questions: is there a new subject after que? Then subjunctive. Is it the same person, or everyone? Then the infinitive.

bites.title: Feeling + que
bites.rule: When you react to what someone else does, put their action in the subjunctive after que: me alegra que, me molesta que, me preocupa que, odio que…
bites.example: Me molesta que hables tan alto.
bites.example_meaning: It bothers me that you talk so loudly.

bites.title: Judgements
bites.rule: Es importante / necesario / mejor / normal / una pena / increíble + que + subjunctive when a specific person is meant.

bites.title: Same person? Infinitive
bites.rule: No new subject, no que: if you are the one who acts, or you mean everyone, use the infinitive.
bites.example: Me alegra verte. Es importante dormir.
bites.example_meaning: I'm glad to see you. Sleep is important.

bites.title: Even if it's true
bites.rule: The subjunctive marks a reaction, not doubt. You know the fact and still say que + subjunctive.
bites.example: Me da pena que estés enfermo.

sorts.title: Que + subjunctive or infinitive?
sorts.why: A new subject after que takes the subjunctive; the same person or people in general take the infinitive.

sorts.title: Fact or reaction?

items.text: Me da pena que estés cansado.

sorts.why: Knowing or stating a fact takes the indicative; a feeling or judgement about it takes the subjunctive, even when it is true.

spots.why: A feeling about someone else: me alegra que + subjunctive.
Es importante que + subjunctive; -ir dormir changes o to u in nosotros.

spots.sentence: Me encanta que tú vienes a cenar.
spots.why: Me encanta que + subjunctive, built on vengo.

spots.sentence: Es normal que los niños están cansados.
Odio que mi jefe me habla así.
spots.why: Odio que + subjunctive when someone else acts.

builds.text: Me da pena que no vengas.
builds.meaning: It makes me sad that you're not coming.

builds.text: Es mejor que llames a tu madre.
builds.meaning: It's better if you call your mother.

realm.content:
## Sentimientos en Eldmark

Every hero has feelings about the party: **me alegra que la maga venga**, **me preocupa que el dragón despierte**, **es importante que el paladín proteja al grupo**. When someone else acts, use **que** + subjunctive. When you act, or everyone does, use the infinitive: **me encanta luchar**, **es mejor descansar antes de la mazmorra**.

vocabulary.example: Me alegra que la elfa cure al grupo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm glad the elf heals the group.

vocabulary.example: Me preocupa que el dragón despierte.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It worries me that the dragon might wake up.

vocabulary.example: Es importante que el paladín proteja a la maga.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's important that the paladin protects the mage.

vocabulary.example: Odio que los orcos ataquen de noche.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hate it when the orcs attack at night.

vocabulary.example: Es mejor que vayamos por el Bosque Umbrío.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's better if we go through the Bosque Umbrío.

vocabulary.example: Es normal que la mazmorra esté oscura.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's normal for the dungeon to be dark.

vocabulary.example: Es mejor que no entres solo en la mazmorra.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's better if you don't go into the dungeon alone.

vocabulary.example: Me encanta que el botín sea de oro.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I love it that the loot is gold.

vocabulary.example: Es increíble que tu montura vuele.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's amazing that your mount flies.

bites.title: Sentimientos de héroe
bites.rule: Feelings and judgements about another hero take que + subjunctive; about yourself or everyone, the infinitive.
bites.example: Me alegra que el enano venga. Me alegra luchar.
bites.example_meaning: I'm glad the dwarf is coming. I'm glad to fight.

listening.text: Me alegra que el enano venga.
listening.meaning: I'm glad the dwarf is coming.

listening.text: Es importante que llevemos una poción.
listening.meaning: It's important that we take a potion.
listening.note: New word: la poción = the potion.

listening.text: Me molesta que el mago hable tanto.
listening.meaning: It annoys me that the wizard talks so much.

listening.text: Es increíble que el dragón duerma aquí.
listening.meaning: It's amazing that the dragon sleeps here.
listening.note: New word: el dragón = the dragon.

listening.text: Es mejor descansar antes de la mazmorra.
listening.meaning: It's better to rest before the dungeon.

builds.text: Es necesario que el paladín luche.
Me encanta que tengas una montura.
builds.meaning: I love it that you have a mount.

spots.sentence: Me alegra que la maga está aquí.
spots.why: A feeling about someone else: que + subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Es mejor que el orco vuelve a Emberhold.

sorts.title: Fact or feeling in Eldmark?

items.text: Me preocupa que el orco ___ (tener) hambre.
Es una pena que la poción ___ (ser) tan cara.

sorts.why: Knowing or reporting a fact takes the indicative (duerme, tiene, está); a feeling or judgement about it takes the subjunctive (duerma, tenga, sea).

quiz.explanation: A worry about what someone else (the dragon) does: me preocupa que + subjunctive. Despertar keeps its e to ie change: despierte.
hints: Different subject after que.
Start from despierto and swap -o for -e: despierte.

quiz.explanation: Es increíble que + subjunctive. Volar changes o to ue in the él form: vuele.
hints: Present subjunctive, él form.
Start from the yo present (o to ue) and swap -o for -e.

conversations.title: Before the dungeon
conversations.scenario: Mirela the mage and Durgo the dwarf get ready at the gates of a dungeon near Frostmarch.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Durgo, me alegra que vengas a la mazmorra conmigo.
lines.meaning: Durgo, I'm glad you're coming to the dungeon with me.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Claro. Pero me preocupa que el dragón esté despierto.
lines.meaning: Of course. But it worries me that the dragon might be awake.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Es normal que tengas miedo. Es tu primera mazmorra.
lines.meaning: It's normal for you to be scared. It's your first dungeon.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: No es miedo. Odio que los dragones me quemen la barba.
lines.meaning: It's not fear. I hate it when dragons burn my beard.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Entonces es mejor que lleves una poción de hielo.
lines.meaning: Then it's better if you take an ice potion.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Buena idea. Y es importante salir antes de la noche.
lines.meaning: Good idea. And it's important to get out before nightfall.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Me encanta que seas tan prudente, Durgo.
lines.meaning: I love it that you're so careful, Durgo.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Y a mí me alegra luchar a tu lado.
lines.meaning: And I'm glad to fight at your side.

meadowbrook.content:
## Sentimientos en la granja

On the farm everyone reacts to everyone: **me alegra que llueva** (good for the crops), **a Rosa le preocupa que las gallinas no coman**, **es importante que cosechemos antes del otoño**. Doing it yourself, or talking about everyone? Use the infinitive: **me encanta plantar fresas**.

vocabulary.example: Me alegra que las fresas crezcan tan rápido.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm glad the strawberries are growing so fast.

vocabulary.example: Es importante que cosechemos el maíz antes de la lluvia.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's important that we harvest the corn before the rain.

vocabulary.example: Me preocupa que la vaca no quiera comer.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It worries me that the cow won't eat.

vocabulary.example: Es una pena que la tienda de semillas cierre los domingos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's a shame the seed shop closes on Sundays.

vocabulary.example: El alcalde está contento de que vengas al festival.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mayor is happy that you're coming to the festival.

vocabulary.example: Es increíble que la cosecha sea tan grande.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's amazing that the harvest is so big.

vocabulary.example: Me encanta que las calabazas estén listas para el festival.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I love it that the pumpkins are ready for the festival.

vocabulary.example: Es necesario que Leo arregle la valla antes del invierno.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo needs to fix the fence before winter.

bites.title: Sentimientos en la granja
bites.rule: Your feelings about a neighbour, a crop or the weather take que + subjunctive; your own actions take the infinitive.
bites.example: Me alegra que llueva. Me encanta plantar.
bites.example_meaning: I'm glad it's raining. I love planting.

listening.text: Me alegra que llueva hoy.
listening.meaning: I'm glad it's raining today.

listening.text: Es necesario que plantemos las semillas.
listening.meaning: We need to plant the seeds.
listening.note: New word: la semilla = the seed.

listening.text: A Leo le molesta que el río esté tan bajo.
listening.meaning: It bothers Leo that the river is so low.

listening.text: Es mejor pescar por la tarde con Leo.
listening.meaning: It's better to fish in the afternoon with Leo.

listening.text: Es una pena que la oveja esté enferma.
listening.meaning: It's a shame the sheep is ill.
listening.note: New word: la oveja = the sheep.

builds.text: Me encanta que Nora cultive fresas.
builds.meaning: I love it that Nora grows strawberries.

builds.text: Es importante que cuidemos las gallinas.
builds.meaning: It's important that we look after the hens.

spots.sentence: Me alegra que la cosecha es buena.
spots.why: A feeling about the harvest: que + subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Es normal que las vacas tienen hambre.

sorts.title: Que + subjunctive or infinitive on the farm?
sorts.why: If someone else acts, use que + subjunctive. If you act, or it's about everyone, use the infinitive.

quiz.prompt: A Rosa le preocupa que no ___ (llover) este verano.
quiz.explanation: Le preocupa que + subjunctive. Llover changes o to ue: llueva.
hints: Present subjunctive of llover.
Llover changes o to ue, and -er verbs take -a in the subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Es mejor ___ por la mañana, cuando no hace calor. (advice for every farmer)
quiz.explanation: Advice for everyone in general takes the infinitive: es mejor trabajar. A specific person would need que + subjunctive (que trabajes).
hints: General advice, no specific person.

rustwake.content:
## Sentimientos en el páramo

Out on the wasteland feelings run high: **me preocupa que el agua no esté filtrada**, **a Marta le molesta que pagues con tuercas oxidadas**, **es importante que el robot jardinero funcione**. About yourself or everybody? Use the infinitive: **es mejor viajar de día**.

vocabulary.example: Me molesta que el radiorreloj solo ponga música vieja.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It annoys me that the wrist radio only plays old music.

vocabulary.example: Es necesario que reparemos la antena.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We need to repair the antenna.

vocabulary.example: Me da pena que el perro guardián esté solo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It makes me sad that the guard dog is alone.

vocabulary.example: Es increíble que el robot jardinero cultive tomates.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's amazing that the gardener robot grows tomatoes.

vocabulary.example: Me encanta que Leo el buscador encuentre discos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I love it that Leo the scavenger finds records.

vocabulary.example: Es normal que el escarabajo gigante tenga hambre.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's normal for the giant beetle to be hungry.

vocabulary.example: Me alegra que tengas tantas tuercas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm glad you have so many nuts.

vocabulary.example: Odio que el páramo sea tan seco.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hate how dry the wasteland is.

vocabulary.example: Es una pena que la cúpula esté cerrada.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's a shame the Dome is closed.

bites.title: Sentimientos en el páramo
bites.rule: A reaction to what someone or something else does takes que + subjunctive, even out on the wasteland.
bites.example: Es increíble que el robot funcione.
bites.example_meaning: It's amazing that the robot works.

listening.text: Me alegra que llegues al mercado.
listening.meaning: I'm glad you're getting to the market.

listening.text: Es importante beber agua filtrada.
listening.meaning: It's important to drink filtered water.

listening.text: Me preocupa que el capataz Ruiz esté enfadado.

listening.meaning: It's a shame the petrol station is empty.
listening.note: New word: la gasolinera = the petrol station.

listening.text: Odio que el viento traiga ceniza.
listening.meaning: I hate it when the wind brings ash.
listening.note: New word: la ceniza = the ash.

builds.text: Es necesario que caminemos de noche.
builds.meaning: We need to walk at night.
I love listening to the radio.

spots.sentence: Me da pena que la cabra está perdida.
spots.why: A feeling about the goat: que + subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Es importante que Marta cambia agua por tuercas.

sorts.title: Fact or reaction on the wasteland?

items.text: Me encanta que Marta venda tónicos.
Es increíble que el robot funcione.
Ruiz dice que la antena está rota.
Es una pena que la antena esté rota.

sorts.why: Stating or reporting a fact takes the indicative; a feeling or judgement about it takes the subjunctive, even when it's true.

quiz.prompt: Es necesario que nosotros ___ el radiorreloj antes de salir.
quiz.explanation: Es necesario que + subjunctive for specific people (nosotros). Reparar becomes reparemos.
hints: A specific subject after que.
-ar verbs switch to -e.

quiz.prompt: Me da pena que el perro guardián no ___ (tener) dueño.
quiz.explanation: Me da pena que + subjunctive. Tener builds on tengo: tenga.
hints: Present subjunctive, él form.
Start from the yo present, with its g, and swap -o for -a.
